market_holds: Spot $1.21 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-13 18:14 UTC), 89% below the 52-week high and 7% above the low. It has fallen steadily from about $2.0 at the Q2 print (2026-08-13) to $1.13 by mid-October. There was a brief bounce to $1.38 on 2026-10-21 around the McKinney/Centennial sale-leasebacks, then a fade: -6.9% over 5 days, +4.3% over 20 days. The option chain is unusable (16 contracts of open interest, no two-sided quotes), so there is no implied move. The usual move is a median 3.85% absolute over 8 prints, 3 of them up. The two large drops (-21% in Nov 2025, -40% in Jan 2026) came with equity-offering or financing news. The last three prints moved -1.5%, -3.1% and +4.6%. Realised volatility is 96% annualised. Analyst coverage is 1-2 brokers with stale numbers (e.g. stockanalysis shows FY26 EPS of -$0.02 against a first-half loss of about -$0.60), so there is no live consensus. Short interest is 4.82m shares, 8.6% of float, 12.2 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30, from the sweep). The stock trades on liquidity, financing and dilution (ATM in place since June 2026, Yorkville convertible) and on venue openings, not on quarterly revenue (about $5m a quarter).
view: This is a distressed, financing-driven microcap, and the Q3 FY26 print (to Sep 30) will mostly restate things the 8-Ks already made public. Cash was $16.3m at June 30 after $133m spent in the half. Since then the company has raised a $20m Ryan bridge loan (July), a $25m Yorkville convertible of which only $12.5m was funded, with the holdback used to pay down principal effective Sep 30, a $5m Aramark preferred tranche (Oct 15), and the $60m McKinney and $7.5m Centennial sale-leasebacks (Oct 16-20), out of which the Ryan note was repaid. All of that was in 8-Ks by Oct 26. So the Sep 30 balance sheet will look thin, but the subsequent-events note will show new liquidity the market has seen already. The open questions the release and call can still answer: (1) the $150m CBRE C-PACE financing. It was 'identified' on Jul 9, management said in August it would close in Q3 2026, and no 8-K announcing a close has appeared. Meanwhile the company did the sale-leasebacks it had said it would move away from, which suggests C-PACE has slipped. The call could announce a close (upside) or a further delay or smaller amount (downside). (2) Broken Arrow already slipped from 'fall 2026' to a December reduced-capacity 'Winter Preview', which is public. (3) Share count and ATM use will show on the 10-Q cover. (4) Yorkville monthly installments of $5m plus a 20% premium started around Oct 14. On a payment failure they convert at 95% of the low VWAP, which is an overhang. The President left on Oct 13 and the CEO received a 5m-share grant on Oct 20, both public. On balance the print is more likely to confirm the bearish financing story than to break it. But most of it is in the 8-Ks, the stock is already at all-time lows with 12 days to cover, and a C-PACE close announced at the print would trigger a sharp short-covering bounce. I lean slightly down and not far enough to act.

recommendation.reason: The financing and dilution facts that drive this stock were all disclosed in 8-Ks dated Aug-Oct 2026, and the tape has followed them down. The one real open question, whether the $150m C-PACE financing has closed, could go either way at the release, and I found no public trace of how it stands. A mild negative lean (ATM dilution, Yorkville overhang, loss guidance) does not reach the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An announcement in the release or call that the $150m C-PACE financing has closed or has a firm date would turn me long. A new equity raise or a going-concern doubt reinstated in the 10-Q would make me a confident short.

self_critique: The bearish financing story is clear, and a deeply distressed name with an ATM and Yorkville paper often drifts down through a print. Q3 2025 fell 21%. A thin Sep 30 cash balance printed in black and white could hit retail holders even though the October proceeds are public, which argues for a lower p_up. Against that, the stock is at all-time lows with 12 days to cover and has absorbed months of bad news, and a pre-arranged positive financing update timed to the call is a classic microcap move. The gap could be large either way, so a few points away from 50 is all the evidence supports.
approach_notes: The 'freshest data first' rule and reading the 8-Ks myself paid: they showed that the liquidity events are already disclosed, and that C-PACE is the one unresolved item. The 'priced-in is a claim to prove' test was hard to apply with no consensus or option chain; the tape's response to the October 8-Ks was the only usable evidence.
